1	# WP-004: Orchestrator Runs Flicker-Free DOM Patching and Scroll Preservation
     2	
     3	## Plan Context
     4	
     5	Make the GUI project detail page fully dynamic by adding periodic polling for all project-related data (WP statuses, synthesis availability, project status, health badge) and fix the orchestrator runs section to update without flicker or scroll position loss by using targeted DOM patching instead of full innerHTML rebuilds.
     6	
     7	## Description
     8	
     9	Refactor the orchestrator runs section update path to use targeted DOM patching for the active-run status card and to preserve scroll position during structural re-renders, eliminating the visible flicker caused by full `innerHTML` rebuilds of the runs list every 5 seconds.
    10	
    11	## Scope
    12	
    13	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/project-detail.js` — modifications to `renderRunsList` function and active-run update logic
    14	- `mcp-server/tests/gui/project-detail-scroll.test.ts` — unit tests for scroll preservation logic
    15	
    16	## Deliverables
    17	
    18	- Modified `renderRunsList` that saves `scrollTop` of the `#orchestrator-runs-section` element (or nearest scrollable ancestor) before any innerHTML rebuild and restores it afterward
    19	- Status card container tagged with a known ID (`orch-status-card-container`) on first render
    20	- In-place status card update path: when runs list structure hasn't changed (same filenames, same active run), update the status card HTML via `innerHTML` on just the card container, update badge text and elapsed time directly — do NOT rebuild the runs list or log preview
    21	- Structural re-render path: when runs list structure HAS changed (new run appeared, active run became inactive), perform full `renderRunsList` rebuild with scroll preservation
    22	- Unit test file `project-detail-scroll.test.ts` covering: scrollTop save/restore around innerHTML rebuild, scrollTop preservation when only status card updates, scrollTop reset when runs list structure changes
    23	
    24	## Dependencies
    25	
    26	- WP-003 — Combined Poll Function and Polling Mode State Machine (depends on WP-001, WP-002)
    27	
    28	## Acceptance Criteria
    29	
    30	1. The orchestrator runs section updates without visible flicker — no full-page flash during data-only polls
    31	2. Scroll position in the orchestrator runs section is preserved across poll updates that don't change the runs list structure
    32	3. The status card (Running badge, elapsed time, PID, progress) updates in-place without rebuilding the entire runs list
    33	4. When a new run appears or the active run becomes inactive, the runs list performs a structural re-render but saves and restores scroll position
    34	5. Log preview widgets continue to function correctly — they are NOT destroyed/recreated during data-only status card updates
    35	6. The kill button, dismiss button, and all existing run-event handlers continue to work after in-place status card updates
    36	7. All unit tests in `project-detail-scroll.test.ts` pass
    37	
    38	## Active Pipeline Stages
    39	
    40	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    41	
    42	## Estimated Complexity
    43	
    44	Medium
    45	
    46	## Rationale
    47	
    48	The current `renderRunsList` performs a full `innerHTML` rebuild every 5 seconds, which tears down all DOM nodes (including log preview widgets), causes a visible flash, and loses scroll position. Separating data-only updates (status card, elapsed time) from structural changes (run count change) allows the common case to be flicker-free while still handling rare structural changes gracefully.
    49	
    50	## Rejected Approaches
    51	
    52	- **Incremental insert/remove of run rows** — row-level incremental DOM operations add complexity for a rare event (a new run appearing mid-session); full re-render with scroll preservation is cleaner for structural changes.
    53	
    54	## Notes
    55	
    56	This WP depends on WP-003 because the orchestrator runs updates are triggered by the combined poll function. The existing `_pdLogPreviewCleanups` drain logic must be preserved: log preview cleanups should be drained before structural re-renders but NOT before data-only status card updates. The `orch-status-card-container` ID must be unique and stable across renders. The existing active-run queue-match and toolbar synchronization behavior must be preserved — resume/kill affordances and run-state transitions must continue to behave exactly as they do today.
